Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3469; unblamable:--blameless.
BiblicalUsage: Peter uses it once, at the end of his letter: seeing that we look for new heavens and a new earth, be diligent to be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless. The word shares its root with the one for a lamb without blemish — a life with nothing on it that can be blamed.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Peter's call to live clean while we wait for the day of God.
